question: Let $A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & x \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ x & 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$. Find the values of $x$ for which $|A| = 0$.
explanation:
Compute the determinant using the first row.
$|A| = 2\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{vmatrix} - 1\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ x & 2\end{vmatrix} + x\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 \\ x & 1\end{vmatrix}$.
Compute minors.
$\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{vmatrix} = 3$.
$\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ x & 2\end{vmatrix} = 2 - x$.
$\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 \\ x & 1\end{vmatrix} = 1 - 2x$.
Substitute them.
$|A| = 2(3) - (2 - x) + x(1 - 2x)$.
$= 6 - 2 + x + x - 2x^2$.
$= 4 + 2x - 2x^2$.
Set determinant equal to zero.
$4 + 2x - 2x^2 = 0$.
Divide by $2$.
$2 + x - x^2 = 0$.
Rearrange.
$x^2 - x - 2 = 0$.
Factorize.
$(x - 2)(x + 1) = 0$.
Thus $x = 2$ or $x = -1$.
